title: RMS Voltage, RMS Current and Real Power in Fixed Point
statement:
An energy meter samples voltage and current over one whole mains cycle. From the samples it must compute **RMS voltage**, **RMS current** and **real power**. There is no floating point unit, so all of it is integer arithmetic.

## Your function

```
void rms_power(const int16_t *v, const int16_t *i, size_t n,
               uint32_t *vrms_out, uint32_t *irms_out, int32_t *p_out);
```

`v[k]` and `i[k]` are signed 16-bit ADC counts taken at the same instant. `n` is at least 1 and at most 4096.

Compute, in raw counts (no scaling):

```
vrms = isqrt( floor( sum(v[k]*v[k]) / n ) )
irms = isqrt( floor( sum(i[k]*i[k]) / n ) )
p    = sum(v[k]*i[k]) / n          (division truncates towards zero)
```

`isqrt(x)` is the **exact floor of the square root** of `x`, as an integer. Do the mean first, then the square root, exactly as written. **Do not use floating point.**

The harness reads `n` and then `n` lines of `v i`, and prints `vrms irms p`.

## Watch out

- `v[k]*v[k]` can reach 2<sup>30</sup>. Summed over 4096 samples it reaches 2<sup>42</sup>. A 32-bit accumulator overflows. Use 64-bit.
- `v[k]*i[k]` is **signed**, and so is the sum. A negative real power is real: energy is flowing the other way.
- Do not take a floating-point `sqrt`. It cannot be trusted to be exact for large 64-bit values.
- `-32768 * -32768` is `1073741824`, which still fits an `int32_t`. A single product is fine. The sum is not.

tests.name: one sample
tests.description: RMS of a single value is its magnitude. Power is the product.

tests.name: current lagging by a quarter cycle
tests.description: Real power is close to zero: all the current is reactive.

tests.name: current in antiphase
tests.description: Power is negative. Do not clamp it to zero.

tests.name: the mean is not a whole number
tests.description: 34 / 3 is 11.33 and floors to 11, whose root floors to 3.

tests.name: full-scale negative
tests.description: The product of two negatives is a large positive.

tests.name: just below a perfect square
tests.description: sum of squares is 381, mean 95, isqrt 9, not 10.

tests.name: the longest buffer, no overflow
tests.description: Sum of squares is about 4.4e12. It does not fit in 32 bits.
